title: Named crew catalog
description: Top-level catalog of saved staffing blocks (named crews). Every crew carries a required `kind` discriminator with exactly two conditional shapes, encoded as JSON Schema `if/then` (Chief round 9, D86/D87): `interactive` crews carry a supervisor route, worker routes per role, a reviewer route, and a nonempty escalation ladder, exactly as this schema has always required; `governed` crews reference the Auto-Orch crew by name (`source: auto-orch/crews.yaml`, `crew_name`), carry `supervisor: {kind: engine, owner: auto-orch}` instead of a route, map the recorded stages and the governed `primary`/`reviewer`/`judge` role names to routes through `worker_routes`, and record `escalation: not-recorded` as the explicit absence of a ladder — no supervisor route or identity ladder is ever invented for a governed crew. The reserved `auto` placeholder is `kind: interactive`, `authority: policy`, with its route-bearing fields unset and marked `computed`. Route references are opaque catalog ids resolved against the route catalog; this schema defines shape only and encodes no selection, ranking, probability, class metadata, or model preference. The authority value `policy` is reserved for the computed `auto` placeholder saved block and means the staffing system's choice.

crews.description: Saved staffing blocks. Each crew has a stable crew_id and a required `kind` of `interactive` or `governed`; crew_id `auto` is the single reserved placeholder id and pairs only with authority `policy`.

routeRef.description: Opaque reference to a route_id in the route catalog. Shape only: never resolved or interpreted here.

roleKey.description: Role name keying a worker route binding.

crew_id.description: Stable identifier for this saved staffing block. The reserved id `auto` marks the computed placeholder block and requires authority `policy`.

kind.description: Required discriminator. `interactive`: a human-supervised crew with a real supervisor route, per-role worker routes, a reviewer route, and a nonempty escalation ladder. `governed`: a crew referenced from the Auto-Orch crew catalog whose supervisor is the Auto-Orch loop plus the agent-orch engine, never a model route.

supervisor_route.description: Interactive crews only. Opaque route catalog id used for the supervisor role. A governed crew must never carry this field: its supervisor is the engine, not a model route.

worker_routes.description: Worker routes keyed by role. Each role binds exactly one nonempty, duplicate-free, order-significant list of opaque route references; the list order is the role's route preference order. A single route must still be encoded as a one-element array. For interactive crews the keys are the crew's roles; for governed crews the keys carry the recorded Auto-Orch stage bindings plus the governed `primary`/`reviewer`/`judge` role names that have a recorded route.

reviewer_route.description: Interactive crews only. Opaque route catalog id used for the reviewer role. A governed crew maps its governed reviewer through `worker_routes` instead.

escalation_ladder.description: Interactive crews only. Ordered, nonempty escalation ladder of opaque route catalog ids. Array order is the ladder order. A governed crew must never carry this field: it records `escalation: not-recorded` instead of an invented one-rung identity ladder.

source.description: Governed crews only. The Auto-Orch crew catalog the crew is referenced from, fixed by contract.

crew_name.description: Governed crews only. The referenced crew's name in the Auto-Orch crews.yaml source.

supervisor.description: Governed crews only. Exactly `{kind: engine, owner: auto-orch}`: the supervisor is the Auto-Orch loop plus the agent-orch engine, not a model route.

escalation.description: Governed crews only. Explicit absence of an escalation ladder; the governed crew resolver never escalates. Never a one-rung identity ladder invented to satisfy a nonempty rule.

computed.description: Reserved for the `auto` placeholder block: marks that its route-bearing fields are unset because the staffing system computes them at run time.

governed_ref.description: Ordinary named interactive crews only. Optional nonempty reference preserved verbatim on the block. Explicitly forbidden on governed crews and on the reserved `auto` placeholder.

authority.description: Who set this block: `lee` pins or overrides; `chief` chooses under delegated managerial authority; `policy` is reserved for the computed `auto` placeholder and means the staffing system's choice.

evidence_ref.description: Nonempty reference to the evidence backing this saved block.

allOf.description: Authority `policy` is reserved for the computed placeholder block: it requires crew_id `auto`.

crew_id `auto` is the placeholder block: it requires authority `policy`, so a named crew (authority `lee` or `chief`) can never use the `auto` id and the placeholder can never carry `lee` or `chief` authority.

Interactive special case for the reserved placeholder: crew_id `auto` is `kind: interactive`, `authority: policy`, with its route-bearing fields unset and marked `computed` (Chief round 9). This branch applies only to the reserved id; every other interactive crew keeps today's full route-bearing shape.
The `computed` marker is reserved for the `auto` placeholder: it can never appear on a named crew.

Ordinary interactive crews (any crew_id other than the reserved `auto`) keep today's shape: supervisor route, worker routes per role, reviewer route, and a nonempty escalation ladder are all required, and no governed-only field may appear.

Governed crews reference the Auto-Orch crew by name, carry the engine supervisor instead of a supervisor route, map the recorded stages and the governed primary/reviewer/judge role names to routes through worker_routes, and record `escalation: not-recorded`. They must never carry `supervisor_route`, `reviewer_route`, or an escalation ladder.
